4 ارذّت السَّمَآءُ , (T, S, M, A, K,) inf. n. إِرْذَادٌ; (T, TA;) and ↓ رَذَّت , (A, K,) inf. n. رَذَاذٌ, (TA,) or رُذَاذٌ; (so in the TT as from the T;) The sky rained, or let fall, such rain as is termed رَذَاذ [explained below]. (T, S, M, A, K.) And بَاتَتِ السَّمَآءُ تُرِذُّنَا The sky during the night rained upon us, or let fall upon us, such rain as is so termed. (A.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] ارذّ السِّقَآءُ, (inf. n. as above, T,) (tropical:) The water-skin, or milk-skin, exuded, or let flow, what was in it. (T, A, L, K.) And ارذّت الشَّجَّة (tropical:) The wound in the head flowed with what was in it. (T, A, L, K.) And ارذّت العَيْنُ بِمَائِهَا (tropical:) The eye flowed with its water. (T, A, L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
